name: Question 10
problem: Calculate the circulation $Γ$ of the vector field $F(x,y)=\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation $25{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=25$ oriented counterclockwise.
worked_solution:
First, we write the equation of our curve as

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{1}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{5}^{2}}=1.
$$

The closed curve $C$ is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes $1$ and $5,$ respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

$$
r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j,\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

The circulation $Γ$ measures the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along a *closed* curve $C.$
It is given by the formula

$$
Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,y=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.
$$

So,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =\frac{5}{y}\,i+\frac{1}{x}\,j \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\,i+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)+\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\cdot 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & =-1+5 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Γ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }4\,\text{d}t \\  & =4t\,{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =4(2\pi )-0 \\  & =8\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Question 10

Calculate the circulation Γ of the vector field F(x,y)=5yi+1xj along the ellipse C with equation 25x2+y2=25 oriented counterclockwise.

4π
b
−4π
c
8π

Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we write the equation of our curve as

x212+y252=1.

The closed curve C is the ellipse centered at the origin with horizontal and vertical semiaxes 1 and 5, respectively. It can be parameterized in the counterclockwise direction as

r(t)=cos⁡ti+5sin⁡tj,0≤t≤2π.

The circulation Γ measures the total work done by a force F in moving a particle along a closed curve C. It is given by the formula Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫abF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt.

Along the curve C, we have x=cos⁡t,y=5sin⁡t.

So,

F(r(t))=5yi+1xj=1sin⁡ti+1cos⁡tj.

Computing r′(t), we get

r′(t)=ddt(cos⁡t)i+ddt(5sin⁡t)j=−sin⁡ti+5cos⁡tj.

Therefore,

F(r(t))⋅r′(t)=(1sin⁡ti+1cos⁡tj)⋅(−sin⁡ti+5cos⁡tj)=1sin⁡t⋅(−sin⁡t)+1cos⁡t⋅5cos⁡t=−1+5=4.

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

Γ=∮CF⋅dr=∫02πF(r(t))⋅r′(t)dt=∫02π4dt=4t|02π=4(2π)−0=8π
